data.statement: Adopt the existing AudioMancer project into the agentic workflow by discovering likely components under 04_Software/AudioMancer, proposing a repository-wide component map, and then adopting one human-approved component slice at a time without application behavior changes.

acceptance: Likely components are inventoried with supporting evidence; .agentic/components.toml receives a reviewable proposed map; the human approves a component slice before adoption; that slice is documented and baseline-reviewed; every gate stops for approval; and no runtime behavior changes occur.
assumptions: The configured roots and policies in .agentic/workflow.toml are authoritative for this adoption run.
Component boundaries will be inferred from source layout, entry points, dependencies, tests, and existing documentation, and uncertain boundaries will be reported rather than forced.
No application source files will be modified during adoption.
open_questions: Which component should be the first component-adoption slice after the repository map is proposed?
planned_paths: .agentic/knowledge/components/** and 04_Software/AudioMancer/tests/** (only within a later human-approved component-adoption slice)
data.reason: The current work is limited to workflow records and read-only repository discovery, open component selection is safely deferred to the mandatory map approval gate, and behavior changes are prohibited.
recommended_responses: Defer selection until the component-map gate, then adopt one component explicitly approved by the human.
scope: Repository-wide read-only discovery and component-map proposal for 04_Software/AudioMancer; subsequent component-adoption limited to one component selected after human map approval.
data.source: User adoption request and approval to continue on 2026-07-18
data.understanding: Discover the existing AudioMancer repository under 04_Software/AudioMancer, identify evidence-backed component boundaries, propose a repository-wide component map, and then adopt only a human-approved single-component slice through baseline review and delivery. Adoption may update workflow-owned maps, knowledge, requirements, tests, and reports, but must not change runtime product behavior.

data.rationale: The project manifest is the durable coordination point for every downstream workflow and must remain usable without rewriting domain artifacts during repair.
data.requirement: The application shall create, open, validate, save, and metadata-repair a flat project workspace while presenting manifest-derived lifecycle state through the Home flow.
data.verification: Automated focused pytest coverage passed for workspace lifecycle, Home presentation, controller activation, and option locking.

data.rationale: A stable local source record is required before extraction, while replacement must not delete files outside the project.
data.requirement: Before project options are locked, the application shall import or replace one supported source file inside the project root and return normalized source metadata with collision-safe storage.
data.verification: Automated focused pytest coverage passed for supported source copy, metadata, collision handling, and safe replacement.

data.rationale: Exports are delivery views of established workflow artifacts and must neither expose internal AI transaction logs nor become runtime state.
data.requirement: The Home flow shall expose readiness-based external TXT, Markdown, and ZIP exports that project current usable artifacts into operator-facing deliverables without changing the active project.
data.verification: Automated focused pytest coverage passed for export readiness, archive exclusions, external-path enforcement, and Home enablement.

data.rationale: Operators need a portable project backup that cannot recursively include itself or leave a partial final archive.
data.requirement: The Home flow shall create a cancellable external ZIP snapshot of regular project files under one top-level project folder, excluding symlinks and AI transaction logs and publishing the final archive only after successful completion.
data.verification: Automated focused pytest coverage passed for snapshot structure, cancellation cleanup, active-operation blocking, and Home enablement.

data.rationale: A crash or failed replacement must not turn a previously valid project manifest or settings file into a partial payload.
data.requirement: Critical text and JSON persistence shall write a complete same-directory temporary file, flush and synchronize it, atomically replace the destination, and remove temporary files after failure.
data.verification: Automated focused pytest coverage passed for atomic replacement, failure preservation, cleanup, and manifest writer integration.

data.rationale: Containment prevents untrusted project metadata or operator destinations from reading, deleting, overwriting, or recursively archiving files beyond the intended workspace.
data.requirement: Project-relative source and artifact paths shall reject absolute paths, parent traversal, and symlink escapes, and project export or snapshot destinations shall be outside the active project root.
data.verification: Automated focused pytest coverage passed for traversal, symlink escape, and external export or snapshot destinations.
